title: Layers line up with each other while you build
goal: When you are arranging boxes and labels, nothing helps you line them up with each other: dragging only pulls to the edges and middle of the whole picture, and there is no way to align a few layers or space them evenly. Give the arranging job real help.
notes:
Today Snapping.swift only attracts a dragged frame to the canvas edges and the canvas centre; there is nothing between one layer and another, and no align or distribute command anywhere in EditorCommands.swift. Blocked on its decision card. Guides while dragging were built once before, on 2026-07-02, and turned down, so this must not be built without an answer. Whatever the answer, the maths belongs in PhotonzCore with tests, next to Snapping.swift.

Objective: ui-building (the current focus). Deliberately kept at ui-building rather than moved down to the later ui-layout sub epic: this is help for arranging by hand, not auto layout, so it is legal work now. Nothing here gets built before the card is answered.
acceptance: Build whichever answer the decision card returns, and nothing else
Try it: open Photonz Dev, Experiments window, release Next, flag on, draw three rectangles at rough positions, and line them up the way the answer describes
Every move undoes in one step
Audit written under queue/audits/, and anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task

log.note: Waiting on the decision card: which kind of help arranging layers should get, given guides were turned down once before.

decision "When you are arranging layers to build UI, what should help you line them up?" resolved: Both (We should probably also have grid components that can be placed within a component, grid and stack)

Adversarial review before building. (1) Align needs a reference and the selection bounding box is the only one that needs no explaining; one layer selected has nothing to line up with, so the commands grey out rather than quietly aligning to the canvas. Aligning a lone layer inside a frame is the obvious next ask and is filed as a follow-up instead of guessed at. (2) Space evenly means equal GAPS, not equal centres: when buttons differ in width, Photoshop-style centre distribution leaves visibly uneven gaps, and the gap is the thing you can see. (3) What got guides turned down before was noise with no payoff, so this build keeps them to the minimum that pays: at most one line per axis, only for the layer under the pointer, drawn only across the boxes actually involved rather than across the whole picture, and Command drags free the way it already does for measure and region drags. (4) Cut as decorative: live gap badges while dragging, spacing repeat, persistent user guides and rulers. (5) Peers are gathered once at mouse-down, since nothing but the dragged layer moves during a drag, so a crowded document does not cost frame rate. (6) Hidden layers must not attract, because you cannot see what you snapped to; locked layers still do, since the background is locked and its edges are real.

Built both halves the card asked for. Align and Space Evenly over a selection (LayerArrangement in PhotonzCore, TDD): six align buttons and two spacing buttons in a new Arrange section at the top of the inspector, mirrored in the Layer menu under Align and Space Evenly on the design-tool keys. Align lines the selection up with itself, spacing means equal gaps and holds the outer two still, results land on whole points and the whole selection is one undo step. Guides while dragging (Snapping extended with peers, guide spans and snapPeers, TDD): a dragged layer catches the other layers' edges and centres, sits flush against them, draws a line only across the boxes it joins, and Command drags free. Behind next-align-layers, on by default in Next.

Review of the built thing, on the probe. Walked it with Scripts/playtest/align-layers-walk.json: three rough rectangles align to 120, ONE undo puts all three back, spacing holds the ends and evens the gaps to 100 each, a fourth rectangle dragged in catches the column's left edge at 120, and the same drag with Command held lands at 126 with no line. Real window captures, Screen Recording was granted. What is still clumsy: reaching a multi-selection on the picture needs a rubber band, since shift clicking a layer does not add it to the selection, and that is the weakest part of the whole flow. Filed as its own task, along with lining one layer up inside its frame and the user's grid and stack ask from the card.

Align and Space Evenly over a selection (Arrange row in the inspector plus Layer menu rows on the design-tool keys), and a dragged layer now sticks to the other layers with a short line saying what it caught, Command drags free. Behind next-align-layers, on by default in Next. LayerArrangement and the extended Snapping are in PhotonzCore with 18 new tests; Scripts/test.sh green at 1890 tests. Verified on the probe with Scripts/playtest/align-layers-walk.json against real window captures; audit at queue/audits/2026-09-03-align-layers.json. Pushed as b3b8591.
